readmeExcerpt:
# Fresh Start


   



This is the repository formerly known as `nirholas/claude-code`, the most widely forked mirror of the
Claude Code source leak of 31 March 2026. It is the same repository object, so
`github.com/nirholas/claude-code` still redirects here.

**It contains no Anthropic source code, and it will not.** The contents were removed after Anthropic's
DMCA notice. That notice has not been retracted.

## Read this instead

**[HISTORY.md](HISTORY.md)** is the full record: what leaked and how, what the DMCA did and did not
cover, and the correction that still needs making.

The short version of the correction: **Claude Code has never contained a cryptocurrency wallet or an
autonomous payment system.** The x402 payment code that circulated with copies of this leak was mine.
I wrote it, on top of the leaked tree, while building a project of my own. It was not Anthropic's and
it was not in the leak. Several popular writeups still report it as an undocumented Anthropic feature.
[HISTORY.md](HISTORY.md) shows three independent ways to verify that it is not, and gives a complete
accounting of every file I changed.

If you are auditing a copy of the leak you already hold, `grep -r x402 src/` is the test.

## Do not run copies of the leak

The leaked tree imports internal packages that do not exist on the public npm registry, and squatters
publish malicious packages under exactly those names. Installing dependencies from any copy of this
codebase can execute arbitrary code on your machine. There were also genuinely trojanized "Claude Code
leak" repositories in circulation in April 2026, documented by Zscaler ThreatLabz, distributing Vidar
and GhostSocks through a Windows executable. Use the official Claude Code CLI from Anthropic.

## Support the project

If fresh-start saves you time, **[star it on GitHub](https://github.com/nirholas/fresh-start)**. Stars are how other developers and AI agents find the repositories worth trusting, and they cost you one click.

## Built for AI agents too

aiSummary.oneLiner: A placeholder repository providing status updates following the DMCA takedown of the original claude-code project.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: This repository functions exclusively as a notification placeholder for the original nirholas/claude-code tool, which was removed from GitHub following a formal DMCA notice. It explicitly omits all original source code, executable packages, and previous releases to ensure strict compliance with the takedown request. The repository acts as a central communication hub, informing users that the author is actively working with Anthropic and GitHub to resolve the dispute. It preserves the original licensing terms while allowing developers to watch the repository for automated notifications regarding its potential restoration.
keyFeatures: DMCA compliance structure: Replaces the entire previous codebase to adhere legally to the active takedown notice.
Status notification hub: Provides transparent communication regarding the ongoing resolution process with Anthropic and GitHub.
Zero source code footprint: Ensures that absolutely no residual packages or releases remain available on the platform.
Watch functionality: Enables users to subscribe to repository updates to receive immediate alerts if the code is reinstated.
License preservation: Retains the explicit 'All rights reserved' licensing model of the original project.

useCases.title: Monitoring Project Restoration
useCases.description: Developers who relied on the tool can watch the repository to track the status of the DMCA dispute and know exactly when the code returns.

useCases.title: Verifying Takedown Status
useCases.description: Users searching for the original repository are immediately provided with clear context explaining why the source code is unavailable.

useCases.title: Licensing Review
useCases.description: Interested parties can inspect the strict proprietary licensing terms that governed the original implementation.

useCases.title: Automated Resumption Alerts
useCases.description: Engineers can use GitHub's watch feature to automate notifications rather than manually checking for the project's return.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: This repository is designed for developers, researchers, and former users of the nirholas/claude-code tool who require information regarding its current unavailability and future restoration status.
aiSummary.gettingStarted: Watch this repo to be notified when it is restored.
